subject: Next steps & success criteria: observability, evals, and rollout guardrails
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@skylineai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps & success criteria: observability, evals, and rollout guardrails

Hi Alice,

Thanks for the time this morning — appreciate the context on SkylineAI's production issues. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

Key pain points you shared
- Hard to correlate model performance regressions with code or data changes; teams lack per-request tracing hooks.
- Drift detection is noisy; manual re-evals take days.
- Costs spike unpredictably during nightly batch jobs; need unit-level cost visibility.

Current stack
- Serving: internal inference service built on open-source model runners (custom autoscaling)
- Orchestration: Kubernetes + in-house scheduler
- Observability: Grafana/Prometheus for infra; limited model-level metrics; evals are ad-hoc Jupyter runs

Success criteria (30/60/90)
- 30d: Instrumentation plan — tracing hooks on request/response + example golden prompts for core flows
- 60d: Eval harness + dashboards (latency/cost/per-prompt quality) and regression alerts
- 90d: Canary rollout guardrails + automated fallback to smaller model variants

Immediate next steps
1) I've attached a draft mutual action plan (MAP) with dates — can you review and mark procurement contacts?
2) We'll ship a short dashboard mock (SLOs, per-prompt pass rates, cost per 1k tokens) — Marissa will draft
3) Sergio will propose tracing hook snippets (Python + Go) you can drop into the inference path
4) Agree on 3 golden prompt sets to use as regression baselines

Attachments: SkylineAI_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_v1.docx

Can you confirm the stakeholders (procurement & infra leads) and whether the proposed 30/60/90 milestones look reasonable?

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Park <alice.park@skylineai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@skylineai.com
Date: 2026-08-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & success criteria: observability, evals, and rollout guardrails

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the clear recap. That matches what we discussed. A few notes:
- Procurement contact: procurement@skylineai.com (I've looped them in). They'll need the MAP and standard terms.
- Infra lead is Marcus Lin (marcus.lin@skylineai.com) — please include him for tracing/instrumentation questions.
- For success criteria, push the 60d eval delivery earlier if possible; our release cadence will make a 45d target nicer.

I'm attaching a brief deck (devops-requirements.pdf) that outlines our constraints (VPC peering, no egress to public S3 buckets for logs).

I'll review the MAP and circle back with any redlines by tomorrow EOD.

—Alice
Head of Product
SkylineAI
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & success criteria: observability, evals, and rollout guardrails

Marissa / Sergio —

Looping you two on Alice's note. Highlights for our deliverables:
- Marissa: prioritized dashboard mock (SLOs + per-prompt pass rates + cost per 1k tokens). Make a version that can run with sample metrics (no real Skyline data) and a second slide showing the VPC/egress constraints.
- Sergio: tracing hooks — provide a small Python example that attaches request_id, model_version, prompt_hash to logs and a Go snippet for their inference gateway.
- Ben: I'll ask you to lead the procurement touchpoint once Alice's team returns the MAP.

Quoted from Alice below for reference:
> Thanks for the clear recap. That matches what we discussed.

Can we target drafts by Friday (2026-08-06)? If that's tight, call it out.

Thanks,
Priyom
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & success criteria: observability, evals, and rollout guardrails

Priyom —

Acknowledged. Drafts attached:
- observability-dashboard-mockup.png (3 mock slides consolidated)
- golden-prompts-starter-set.txt (3 prompt groups and expected checks)

Notes:
- Dashboard mock uses synthetic data; includes a 'regression delta' panel that can be wired to alerts when pass_rate drops >5% vs baseline.
- Golden prompts: we'll recommend one 'sanity' set (smoke tests), one 'business-critical' set aligned to their top-3 flows, and one 'edge-case' set for hallucination checks.
- Sergio and I will sync on naming for trace fields so the dashboard pulls the same labels.

I'll set a 30-minute review on Friday with Alice + Marcus (cc'd once proc returns MAP).

–Marissa
Director, Developer Experience
Redwood Inference

Attachments: observability-dashboard-mockup.png, golden-prompts-starter-set.txt
